title: Can Rohit Sharma And Virat Kohli Extend Career Till 2027 World Cup? 'I Believe Age...' | Cricket News - News18
text: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, two of the finest batters of the modern era, have entered the final phase of their playing careers. Both have retired from Tests and T20Is but remain a vital part of India’s ODI setup. However, given both are in their late thirties and the next ODI World Cup is now less than two years away, besides form, age and fitness may also play a key role in whether the Indian team management keeps them in their plans. New Zealand fast bowling great Tim Southee though has tipped Kohli and Rohit Sharma to prolong their careers until the 2027 ODI World Cup provided they maintain their current batting form. Kohli, who has retired from T20Is and Tests, has been in outstanding form, scoring consecutive centuries against South Africa in the ongoing ODI series. Meanwhile, Rohit has also shown he belong to the top level having scored a century and a fifty in his last three matches. “Kohli is arguably the best ever one-day batsman, and if he’s still performing, then why not," Southee told news agency PTI . “Rohit also scored a hundred recently in Australia, so they’re both performing well. As long as they continue contributing to the team, age is just a number." With both batters expected to be around 39 during the 2027 World Cup in South Africa, their future remains a popular topic of discussion. “It’s their decision; if they believe they can still meet the demands of playing at the highest level, then why not. As I mentioned, Virat Kohli is arguably the best one-day batsman ever, and if he’s available for the World Cup, the team will want him to play," Southee remarked. India recently suffered their first home Test series defeat to South Africa in 25 years, a 0-2 whitewash. This loss, coupled with the retirements of Rohit, Kohli, and Ravichandran Ashwin, has signalled a period of transition. Southee, however, did not place much emphasis on India’s setback. “India have lost a lot of experience and are probably in a rebuilding phase. A year ago, they still had a lot of seasoned players when we toured there," Southee said. “Without Rohit, Ashwin, and Kohli, they’ve lost a significant amount of experience and knowledge. It’s now about the other players growing and adapting during this transition period." With PTI Inputs
